title: Lithium-Ion Battery with Silicon-Graphene Composite Anode
abstract: A rechargeable lithium-ion battery comprising a composite anode of silicon nanoparticles embedded in a graphene matrix, a lithium metal oxide cathode, and a solid-state ceramic electrolyte.
claims: A battery anode comprising silicon nanoparticles (10-100nm) in a graphene oxide matrix at 60:40 to 80:20 ratio.
A solid-state electrolyte layer comprising LLZO with ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS/cm.
Manufacturing by ball-milling silicon powder with graphene oxide followed by thermal reduction at 800C.
problem_statement: Conventional graphite anodes limit energy density to ~250 Wh/kg. Silicon offers 10x capacity but suffers 300% volume expansion.
